biography: Angus Fender, hailing from the quiet countryside of Oxfordshire, England, didn't discover racing through a family legacy or karting championships. Instead, his passion ignited during a chance visit to Silverstone at the age of 16. The raw power and visceral roar of the engines captivated him instantly. He began with local club racing in a battered, second-hand Fiesta, funded by a part-time job at a local garage. His early races were a rollercoaster – flashes of brilliance punctuated by costly errors. One defining moment came at Brands Hatch; battling for the lead, he spun off on the last lap, losing the race but earning the respect of seasoned veterans for his aggressive, never-say-die attitude. Now, at 24, Fender is a rising star with Cerulean Blue, striving to refine his raw talent into consistent performance and aiming for a championship title. His journey is far from over, but the flame of passion that ignited at Silverstone burns brighter than ever.
drivingStyle: Fender's driving style is a volatile mix of aggression and finesse. He's known for his daring late-braking maneuvers and his willingness to push the car to its absolute limit, often flirting with the edge of control. While this approach yields spectacular overtakes and impressive lap times, it can also lead to costly mistakes. He is still learning to master tire management and maintain composure under pressure, often succumbing to frustration when faced with setbacks. His raw speed is undeniable, but consistency is the key to unlocking his full potential.

careerHighlight: Winning the Silverstone National Series race in 2022 after starting from the back of the grid due to a qualifying penalty. He carved his way through the field with a series of audacious overtakes, showcasing his raw talent and determination.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the Brands Hatch Grand Prix in 2023 due to overzealous driving. The incident cost him valuable championship points and led to intense criticism from team management.
